NutriVita Foods - Q3 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NutriVita Foods Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if you're using a telephone to ask a question. To withdraw your question, press star then two. We ask that you limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NutriVita Foods' Q3 results. Joining me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Patel, Chief Financial Officer; Mia Chen, Chief Growth Officer; and Raj Singh, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on four key areas: performance in key channels including retail, foodservice, and convenience; progress on sustainability initiatives and goals; market share trends for major brands; and e-commerce sales growth and contribution to total revenue.

First, regarding performance in key channels: We achieved robust organic growth across all three core channels, outpacing category averages through pricing discipline and distribution gains.

Second, concerning progress on sustainability initiatives and goals: We've advanced significantly on sourcing, efficiency, and packaging, driving cost savings and consumer loyalty.

Third, in terms of market share trends for major brands: Our portfolio expanded share across categories and regions, fueled by innovation and premium shifts.

Finally, looking at e-commerce sales growth: Digital channels surged, boosting overall revenue mix and margins.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Patel to provide more detail on our financial results and expand on these areas.

Jordan Patel (CFO):
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3. Net sales were $2.51 billion, representing a 7.2% increase year-over-year on an organic basis. Gross margin was 28.4%, expanded by 110 basis points, impacted positively by mix shift and supply chain efficiencies despite commodity volatility. Operating income was $427 million, and earnings per share were $1.45. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $1.8 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for 8% organic growth, with ROIC above 15%.

To give more color on the key areas Alex highlighted, let me start with our performance across our three core channels—retail, foodservice, and convenience—which collectively drove that 7.2% organic revenue growth in Q3, outpacing the broader F&B category's 4.1% IRI-measured growth. This resilience reflects our disciplined pricing actions—up 5.8% net across channels—premiumization strategy, and targeted distribution gains totaling 1.2 percentage points in ACV. Let me break it down channel by channel, with regional nuances and key initiatives.

Retail remains our largest channel at 52% of net revenues, delivering 6.4% organic growth, with volume up 0.6% and pricing contributing the balance. We gained 120 basis points of market share per Nielsen data, particularly in beverages and snacks, where our flagship brands like HydroSpark, our zero-calorie hydration line, and CrunchVital bars outperformed category averages.

In North America, comparable sales rose 7.9%, fueled by expanded shelf space in club channels—think Costco and Sam's Club—where we launched family-value multipacks that boosted velocity by 14% in high-traffic aisles. We also capitalized on the premium snacking trend, with our organic and plant-based portfolio growing 15.2%, mirroring the explosive rise seen with KIND bars or RXBAR under Mondelez. E-commerce was a bright spot, up 22% via Amazon and Walmart.com, supported by our AI-driven digital shelf optimization, which improved search rankings and out-of-stocks by 30%.

Europe presented headwinds, with flat volumes due to 9% inflation compressing consumer wallets—similar pressures hitting Unilever and Danone—but our 4.2% pricing helped deliver 3.1% growth. Here, we're leaning into regulatory tailwinds like the UK's HFSS reforms by reformulating for lower sugar, targeting a 20% reduction in added sugars across our kids' portfolio by FY25. APAC was stellar at +11%, driven by e-commerce penetration in China via Tmall and our new aseptic packaging for ready-to-drink teas, capturing share from local players like Uni-President.

Strategically, we're accelerating "right-the-shelf" initiatives, reallocating space from low-velocity SKUs to high-margin innovations like our functional mushroom-infused coffees, which have already hit 85% distribution in U.S. grocery.

Foodservice, at 28% of revenues, posted 4.7% organic growth—our strongest quarter since pre-COVID—though still lagging on-premise traffic down 2.1% per Black Box Intelligence data. Case volume grew 1.8%, bolstered by away-from-home consumption rebounding as consumers traded up from home prep amid busy back-to-school and holiday prep seasons.

U.S. QSR partnerships were key: McDonald's and Yum! Brands chains accounted for 40% of our volume surge, with our new single-serve sauce pods and portion-control snack packs reducing food waste by 18% for operators—a direct response to Sysco-reported labor shortages and menu simplification trends. Pricing held firm at +6.2%, preserving margins despite commodity volatility in dairy and proteins.

In Latin America, growth accelerated to 9.4% on robust casual dining recovery in Brazil and Mexico, where we're supplying plant-based alt-meats to chains like Giraffas, tapping the 25% CAGR in that segment per Euromonitor. Europe lagged at +1.2%, pressured by energy costs and strikes, but our sustainability push—100% recyclable bulk packaging—secured preferred supplier status with Compass Group. Challenges persist from operator deleveraging, so we're investing in value-engineered tiers, like our "QSR Essentials" line mirroring Heinz's ketchup pouches, targeting 10% tonnage uplift in FY24.

Our tech edge here includes IoT-enabled inventory forecasting with distributors like US Foods, cutting stockouts by 25% and enabling just-in-time delivery.

Convenience, representing 20% of revenues, was our growth engine at 10.3% organic—nearly double the channel's 5.6% NACS benchmark—driven by 4.2% volume expansion from on-the-go snacking and energy boosts. Fuel demand recovery post-summer slump lifted basket sizes, with our products in 62% of transactions per Kantar data.

North America led with 12.1% growth, as 7-Eleven and Circle K rollouts of our new energy chews—formulated with nootropics akin to Red Bull's focus on functional benefits—drove 28% category share gains in coolers. We optimized secondary displays, achieving 1.5 turns per week versus the channel's 1.1 average. APAC convenience exploded +18%, particularly in Japan's FamilyMart network, where single-serve meal kits rode the "grab-and-go" wave amid urban mobility.

Even in softening Europe, we hit +7.2% via forecourt partnerships with BP and Shell, leveraging electric vehicle charging stations for dwell-time impulse buys. Key initiative: Our vending machine refresh program, deploying 5,000 smart units with contactless payments and personalized recs via app integration, mirroring PepsiCo's Bodega transformation. This is projected to add 300 bps to distribution by year-end.

Across channels, premium and functional segments grew 13.4% versus value's -1.2% decline, validating our portfolio reshape—now 45% premium versus 32% three years ago. Margins expanded on mix shift and supply chain efficiencies, including palm oil hedging amid El Niño risks.

Looking ahead, we expect Q4 channel growth of 6-8%, with convenience leading. Risks include retail deflationary pressures and foodservice traffic softness, but our $250 million innovation pipeline—emphasizing health, sustainability, and convenience formats—positions us to gain share.

Next, as we wrap up these operational highlights, I want to spend a few minutes on one of our key long-term value drivers: sustainability. At NutriVita Foods, sustainability isn't just about compliance or PR—it's embedded in our core operations, driving margin expansion, supply chain resilience, and consumer loyalty in a market where ESG factors now influence 68% of purchasing decisions, per Nielsen's latest F&B sustainability report. We've made significant strides across our three pillars: sustainable sourcing, operational efficiency, and circular packaging. Let me break it down with the latest metrics.

Starting with sustainable sourcing, which accounts for 45% of our $4.2 billion cost of goods sold. Our 2030 goal is 100% responsibly sourced key commodities—cocoa, coffee, palm oil, and sugar. We're at 72% today, up from 55% last year, putting us ahead of peers like Hershey's at 65% for cocoa and Mondelez at 68%. In cocoa, our partnership with the Rainforest Alliance has certified 85% of our volume, sourced primarily from West Africa, where we've invested $15 million in farmer cooperatives in Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana. This has reduced deforestation risk by 40% in our supply chain, as verified by our third-party audits from SGS. Coffee progress is equally strong: 78% Rainforest Alliance-certified Arabica from Colombia and Vietnam, with a 12% yield improvement for farmers via our regenerative ag pilots, yielding $2.5 million in procurement savings through lower volatility premiums.

Regionally, APAC is our bright spot at 82% compliance, driven by palm oil RSPO certification rates hitting 91% for our snack bars—critical as Indonesia and Malaysia supply 85% of global palm. In EMEA, we're at 68%, challenged by EU Deforestation Regulation headwinds, but we've pivoted 20% of sourcing to Mass Balance certified suppliers like Cargill. The Americas lag at 62%, but our U.S. sugar cane program with Bonsucro has ramped to 75% coverage, mitigating price swings amid Brazil's drought impacts.

Turning to operational efficiency, our water stewardship goal is a 30% reduction in absolute water use by 2025 from our 2019 baseline of 450 million cubic meters annually across 45 plants. We're 28% there already, thanks to closed-loop systems at our Mexico City beverage facility, which recycles 92% of process water—mirroring PepsiCo's playbook but scaled for our $1.8 billion beverage segment. Energy-wise, Scope 1 and 2 emissions are down 22% YoY to 1.2 million metric tons CO2e, with 35% of our grid now renewables via PPAs in Texas and Spain. We're on track for 50% by 2025, accelerated by our $50 million investment in solar at three U.S. plants, delivering a 15% IRR and $8 million annual savings. Scope 3 is tougher—agricultural emissions are 75% of our footprint—but our Science Based Targets initiative-approved roadmap has piloted regenerative farming on 150,000 hectares, boosting soil carbon sequestration by 1.2 tons per hectare, akin to Danone's model.

On circular packaging, we've hit 65% recyclable or compostable packaging by weight, surpassing our 2025 target of 60% and aligning with Unilever's ambitions. Plastic use is down 18% to 120,000 tons annually, with rPET adoption at 45% in our bottled teas and juices—up from 25% in 2022. Our "VitaLoop" initiative, a deposit-return scheme launched in five EU markets, has recovered 72 million bottles YTD, diverting 95% of packaging waste from landfills. This generated $12 million in recycled material revenue, offsetting 3% of packaging COGS. Consumer response? Our sustainable lines—like EcoBean cold brews and RegenBar snacks—grew 24% YoY, capturing 15% market share in the $45 billion premium F&B segment, per Euromonitor.

Strategically, these initiatives are yielding tangible ROI: $45 million in cost avoidances last year from efficiency gains, plus a 5-point gross margin uplift on eco-labeled SKUs, which now represent 28% of revenue. Amid inflation and commodity volatility—cocoa futures up 60% YTD—we're hedging risks through biodiversity credits and supplier financing. Looking ahead, we're committing $100 million over the next three years to nature-positive goals, including a peatland restoration project in Indonesia with The Nature Conservancy, targeting 50,000 hectares by 2027.

We're proud of this progress—verified by our A- CDP Water score and B in Climate—but we know the work continues. Regulatory tailwinds like the EU's CSRD and U.S. SEC climate disclosures will amplify our edge, while consumer trends show 42% willing to pay a 10% premium for verified sustainability, per Kantar.

Before moving on, I'd like to provide some color on market share trends across our major brands, as this remains a key leading indicator for our long-term growth trajectory in the highly competitive Food & Beverage landscape. Our team tracks this rigorously through syndicated data sources like NielsenIQ total universe scans, IRI weekly movers, and Circana's multi-outlet consumer panel, which give us a holistic view of both volume and value share in at-home and away-from-home channels.

Overall, in the $1.2 trillion global F&B market, NutriVita's portfolio of core brands—including our flagship carbonated soft drink Zest Cola, energy shot VitalBoost, snack line CrunchWave, and emerging plant-based dairy alternative NutriMilk—delivered a net market share expansion of 180 basis points year-over-year on a value basis, reaching 8.7% globally. This marks our strongest quarterly gain in three years, driven by a combination of volume resilience amid 4-6% category inflation and strategic premiumization plays. On a volume basis, we eked out a modest 0.4% gain to 7.9%, outperforming the category average decline of 1.2%, which reflects ongoing consumer trade-down pressures in mass channels.

Let me break this down by key categories and regions, with some specific brand callouts.

Carbonated Soft Drinks segment: This $450 billion category continues to face headwinds from health-conscious shifts and regulatory sugar taxes, with total volumes down 2.1% globally. However, our Zest Cola brand bucked the trend, growing volume share by 1.2 points to 25.3% in North America, per Nielsen data through October. This came at the expense of category leader Coca-Cola, which shed 0.5 points to 42.1%, and PepsiCo's core brands, down 0.8 points to 28.4%. Our edge? The rollout of Zest Zero Sugar Reformulated—with 30% less sodium and stevia-sweetened variants—which captured 15% of new low-cal NPD trial according to Kantar Worldpanel. In Europe, where excise duties bit harder post the UK's HFSS regulations, Zest held flat at 12.1% value share, while private labels surged 2.3 points to 22%. We're countering this with our 'Zest Forward' sustainability initiative: 100% rPET bottling across EU markets, boosting brand favorability by 8 points in Millward Brown tracking.

Energy and Functional Beverages: VitalBoost, our #3 energy shot behind Monster and Red Bull, expanded value share by 2.4 points to 14.2% in the $120 billion global energy category, fueled by e-commerce acceleration—now 22% of our U.S. velocity, up from 14% last year. Red Bull's dominance slipped 1.1 points to 38.5% amid premium pricing fatigue, while Celsius—the hot disruptor—gained 3.2 points but remains niche at 7.8%. In APAC, particularly China and India, VitalBoost rode the wellness wave, lifting share 3.1 points to 9.6% via localized formulations like matcha-infused shots compliant with CFDA labeling rules. Key initiative here: Our $150 million investment in precision fermentation tech for natural caffeine isolates, reducing COGS by 12% and enabling 20% faster shelf-life stability—critical for humid markets like Southeast Asia.

Snacks and Healthy On-the-Go: CrunchWave savory snacks grew 1.8 points to 11.4% U.S. value share in the $200 billion category, per IRI, outpacing Frito-Lay's 0.9-point erosion to 32.7% and Mondelez's belVita line holding steady at 5.2%. This was propelled by our air-fried, 50% less oil reformulation, which drove 28% distribution uplift in club channels like Costco and Sam's Club. In LATAM, where inflation hit 25-40% in Brazil and Argentina, we gained 2.7 points to 13.2% volume share by leaning into affordable premium packs—think 20% larger multipacks at parity pricing. Competitor commentary: Hershey's SkinnyPop lost 1.4 points regionally due to supply chain cocoa volatility, underscoring our nut-inclusive diversification strategy.

NutriMilk Plant-Based Dairy: Our fastest grower, up 4.2 points to 6.8% in the $40 billion alt-dairy space. Oat and almond blends captured 18% household penetration in Europe, per Kantar, versus Danone's Silk (down 0.7 to 22.4%) and Chobani's oat entry at 3.1%. This reflects our upstream vertical integration: Partnerships with oat farmers in Scandinavia for traceable, low-water sourcing, aligning with EU Green Deal mandates and lifting ESG scores.

Regional nuances: North America (52% of our revenue): +210 bps aggregate share gain to 12.4%, led by velocity jumps in convenience (C-store share +1.9%) via our VividPay app loyalty program—now 4.5 million active users, driving 15% repeat purchase uplift. Europe (22%): Flat at 7.2%, pressured by volumetric declines but value-protected through premium SKUs (avg +8% ASP). Next up: AI-driven dynamic pricing pilots with Tesco. APAC/LATAM (26%): +320 bps to 6.1%, capitalizing on urbanization and middle-class expansion; Brazil volumes +3.2% via hyper-local flavors like guaraná-infused Zest.

Strategically, these trends validate our 'Thrive30' framework: 30% of R&D spend on health-forward innovation (e.g., probiotics in CrunchWave), 20% on digital DTC channels (our app now 12% of NA sales), and M&A firepower—we closed the $450 million acquisition of Thai functional water brand AquaVita last month, instantly adding 1.1 points in SEA. Looking ahead, we see 2024 share tailwinds from de-stocking normalization and our $300 million capex in regenerative ag for supply chain resilience against climate risks.

We're positioning NutriVita not just to defend share, but to define category growth in a world demanding 'better-for-you' at everyday prices.

Finally, let me highlight one of our fastest-growing channels: e-commerce. This segment continues to be a cornerstone of our digital transformation strategy in the Food & Beverage industry, where consumer preferences have permanently shifted toward convenience, personalization, and seamless omnichannel experiences post-pandemic.

In Q3, e-commerce sales reached $452 million, representing a robust 48% year-over-year growth and a 22% sequential increase from Q2. This marks our 11th consecutive quarter of double-digit e-commerce growth. As a percentage of our total net revenue of $2.51 billion—up 7% YoY—e-commerce now accounts for 18.0%, a significant expansion from 12.1% in Q3 2022 and 15.2% in Q2 2023. For context, this outpaces the broader F&B industry's e-commerce growth rate of around 25-30% YoY, as reported by NielsenIQ and eMarketer, putting us ahead of peers like Mondelez, which saw digital sales contribute about 14% in their last quarter, or Kellogg's at roughly 16%.

Breaking it down by sub-channel, our direct-to-consumer platform, NutriVita Direct, drove 62% of e-commerce revenue at $280 million, up 55% YoY. This was fueled by our subscription model—now with over 1.2 million active subscribers, akin to the HelloFresh playbook—which boasts a 92% retention rate and an average order value of $68, up 12% from last year due to personalized bundling of our high-margin products like protein-packed NutriBars and plant-based ready-to-drink shakes. Marketplace sales via Amazon, Walmart Marketplace, and Instacart contributed the remaining 38% at $172 million, growing 38% YoY, with gross merchandise value hitting $215 million thanks to improved search rankings and sponsored ads.

Regionally, performance was strong across the board, reflecting our tailored go-to-market strategies. In North America, which represents 72% of our e-commerce revenue, sales grew 52% YoY to $325 million. This was propelled by deeper integrations with quick-commerce players like DoorDash and Uber Eats for our fresh meal kits, capturing share in the $15 billion U.S. online grocery market amid inflation-weary consumers trading down to value packs. Europe, at 18% of e-commerce mix, saw 42% growth to $81 million, despite softer consumer sentiment in the UK and Germany. Here, our partnerships with Ocado and Carrefour's digital platforms have been key, navigating EU data privacy regs under GDPR while emphasizing sustainable packaging to meet eco-label demands.

Asia-Pacific delivered explosive 65% YoY growth to $38 million (8% of total e-comm), driven by mobile-first penetration on platforms like Alibaba's Tmall Fresh and Shopee in Southeast Asia. Our localized SKUs, such as low-sugar electrolyte beverages tailored for humid climates, have resonated, with basket sizes 15% above global averages. Emerging markets like Latin America added $8 million, up 35%, via Mercado Libre tie-ups, though logistics headwinds from port congestion capped upside.

Behind these results are several technical initiatives we've aggressively pursued. First, our $150 million investment in cloud-based infrastructure last year—powered by AWS and Snowflake—has enabled real-time inventory synchronization across 15,000 SKUs, reducing stockouts by 28% and boosting conversion rates to 4.2% on NutriVita Direct, well above the F&B industry average of 2.5%. We've rolled out AI-driven recommendation engines, leveraging machine learning models similar to those at PepsiCo's PantryShop, which analyze purchase history to upsell complementary items—lifting AOV by 14% and cross-sell penetration to 45%. On the logistics front, we've optimized cold-chain fulfillment through a partnership with C.H. Robinson, cutting delivery times for perishables like our yogurt parfaits to under 24 hours in 85% of urban markets, while variable costs per order held steady at 22% of revenue despite rising fuel prices.

Strategically, e-commerce isn't just a growth engine—it's a margin expander and data goldmine. DTC channels deliver 450 basis points higher gross margins than traditional retail, at 42% versus 37.5%, due to eliminated slotting fees and trade spend. Lifetime value for e-comm customers now averages $450 over 18 months, a 25% improvement YoY, outstripping customer acquisition costs of $18 via targeted Meta and TikTok campaigns focused on Gen Z's snackification trends. This rich first-party data informs R&D, like our upcoming launch of zero-sugar functional beverages, validated by e-comm A/B testing showing 30% higher demand in urban millennials.

Looking forward, we expect e-commerce to contribute 20-22% of total revenue by year-end 2023 and over 25% by fiscal 2025, supported by $200 million in planned capex for micro-fulfillment centers and AR try-before-you-buy features for meal bundles. Challenges remain, including supply chain volatility for cocoa and nuts—up 20% in costs—and competition from CPG disruptors like Olipop in the better-for-you space. But with our 35% e-comm market share in premium snacks online, per IRI data, we're well-positioned to capture the projected $250 billion global F&B e-commerce opportunity by 2027.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of commodity inflation on your business?

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Good morning, John. We've navigated commodity inflation effectively through our 5.8% net pricing across channels, coupled with hedging strategies for palm oil and cocoa, and the efficiencies from our sustainability initiatives like regenerative farming, which have helped stabilize costs and protect our 110 basis point margin expansion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Lisa Chen (Morgan Stanley):
What are your plans for plant-based innovations and what is the expected revenue impact?

Mia Chen (Chief Growth Officer):
Thanks, Lisa. Our plant-based portfolio, including alt-meats and NutriMilk expansions, is a top priority with a $250 million innovation pipeline behind it. We've seen 24% growth in sustainable lines already, and we expect these to contribute 15-20% incremental revenue in FY24 through deeper QSR penetration and e-commerce bundling, targeting the 25% CAGR in that segment.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Mike Rodriguez (JPMorgan):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Raj Singh (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Mike, thanks for the question. We're leveraging IoT forecasting with partners like US Foods and Sysco to cut stockouts by 25%, alongside just-in-time delivery and diversified sourcing—91% RSPO palm oil in APAC, for instance. Our regenerative ag pilots on 150,000 hectares are building resilience against climate risks like El Niño, keeping disruptions minimal even amid port issues in LATAM.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Emily Park with Barclays. Please proceed.

Emily Park (Barclays):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Jordan Patel (CFO):
Emily, we're reaffirming full-year guidance at 8% organic growth. Q4 channels should see 6-8% growth with convenience leading, e-commerce hitting 20-22% of revenue, continued share gains, and sustainability-driven savings offsetting any traffic softness. We're well-positioned with strong cash flow and innovation momentum.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in NutriVita Foods. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
